_comment: FOR THE CUSTOMER, not applied by this repo.
A custom role definition for Let's Encrypt DNS-01 against Azure DNS. Assign
it to the certificate job's managed identity on each PUBLIC zone listed in
hosted-zones.json. DNS-01 is validated over the public internet, so the
challenge record has to be written where Let's Encrypt can resolve it.
Create it once (Owner or User Access Administrator needed to define a role):
az role definition create --role-definition @example-cert-manager-role.json
after replacing SUBSCRIPTION_ID in AssignableScopes with every subscription
that holds one of your public zones. Then, per zone:
az role assignment create --role 'AKS Manager ACME DNS-01' \
--assignee-object-id <cert job identity principal id> \
--assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal \
--scope <public zone resource id>
Assign at ZONE scope, never record-set scope: lego deletes the
_acme-challenge record after validating, which would delete a record-set
assignment with it.
This is the tightest role in the system: TXT records in one zone, and
nothing else. It cannot create or change A or CNAME records, so it could not
be used to repoint a hostname. It is one step wider than the AWS equivalent,
which is also limited to names beginning _acme-challenge -- Azure RBAC has no
condition on DNS record names.
If you prefer not to maintain a custom role, the built-in DNS Zone
Contributor works too, at the cost of allowing every record type in the zone.
Delete this _comment key before creating the role; az rejects unknown keys.
Name: AKS Manager ACME DNS-01
Description: Write TXT records in a public DNS zone for Let's Encrypt DNS-01 validation. Nothing else.
